score_rationale: Exceptionally strong willingness-to-pay from three premium buyer segments: regulatory affairs consultants, pharmaceutical and medical device compliance officers, and food safety software vendors. FDA publishes all warning letters in a free, scrapable online database at fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/compliance-actions-and-activities/warning-letters with full text, issue date, company name, and violation category. Regulatory intelligence firms like Regulatory Affairs Professionals Society (RAPS), FDLI, and Registrar Corp charge $2,000–$10,000/year for curated FDA enforcement alerts built on this exact public data. The buyer population is massive and high-budget: 50,000+ regulatory affairs professionals, 5,000+ pharma/device companies, 10,000+ food manufacturers, plus law firms and quality consultants. No flat-file competitor exists under $500. Engineering lift is moderate — web scraping with text extraction, then categorization by product type and violation. Zero PII — all enforcement actions are against companies, not individuals. Score is 8 due to high buyer willingness-to-pay, clear differentiation from free FDA web search (bulk CSV format, filterable by year/industry/violation), and validated commercial demand from regulatory intelligence vendors.
summary: A cleaned CSV of all FDA Warning Letters issued from 2020–2025, extracted from the FDA's public Inspections, Compliance, Enforcement, and Criminal Investigations database — freely accessible but not bulk-downloadable from fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/compliance-actions-and-activities/warning-letters. Each record includes the warning letter issue date, company name, company city and state, product category (drugs, biologics, medical devices, food, cosmetics, tobacco, veterinary), violation summary (GMP deviations, adulteration, misbranding, unapproved new drug, 510(k) failure, HACCP non-compliance), responding FDA office (CDER, CDRH, CFSAN, CVM, ORA), and a direct link to the full warning letter PDF. The FDA issues 200–400 warning letters per year across all regulated industries — representing the most serious compliance failures short of product seizure or injunction. Regulatory intelligence platforms like RAPS, RegDesk, and Registrar Corp charge $2,000–$8,000/year for FDA enforcement tracking and alert services built from this same public dataset. A one-time $89 CSV of 6 years of warning letters (1,200–2,400 total records) targets regulatory affairs consultants advising clients on FDA compliance trends, pharmaceutical and medical device quality managers benchmarking competitor inspection outcomes, food safety consultants identifying industry-wide HACCP and sanitation failures, and compliance software vendors (MasterControl, Veeva Vault QMS, ETQ Reliance) seeking prospects with recent FDA enforcement actions.

audience.who: Regulatory affairs consultants (independent and boutique firms like Lachman Consultant Services, Greenleaf Health, Biologics Consulting, ProPharma Group, plus thousands of solo RA consultants) advising pharmaceutical, medical device, and food companies on FDA compliance strategy, using warning letter trend analysis to identify common inspection pitfalls and prove subject-matter expertise to prospects; pharmaceutical and medical device quality assurance and regulatory affairs managers at companies like Pfizer, Merck, Medtronic, Abbott, Stryker, and 5,000+ smaller manufacturers who monitor competitor and industry warning letters to benchmark their own QMS programs and prepare for FDA inspections; food safety and HACCP consultants advising food manufacturers, processors, and importers on FSMA compliance, who use FDA warning letter databases to demonstrate industry violation patterns and justify consulting engagements; compliance software and quality management system (QMS) vendors like MasterControl, Veeva Vault, ETQ Reliance, and Sparta Systems targeting companies with recent FDA warning letters as high-intent prospects for deviation management, CAPA tracking, and document control software; law firms specializing in FDA regulatory defense (Hyman, Phelps & McNamara; King & Spalding; Kleinfeld, Kaplan & Becker) building case law databases and monitoring enforcement trends for client advisories.

data_wanted: FDA Warning Letters database — publicly accessible via https://www.fda.gov/inspections-compliance-enforcement-and-criminal-investigations/compliance-actions-and-activities/warning-letters but not available as bulk CSV download; requires web scraping with rate-limiting and User-Agent identification. Key fields per warning letter: issue date (YYYY-MM-DD), warning letter number (CMS tracking ID), company name (legal entity named in the letter), company city, company state, company country (for foreign manufacturers/importers), product type (Drugs, Biologics, Medical Devices, Food, Dietary Supplements, Cosmetics, Tobacco, Veterinary Products), issuing office (CDER=Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, CDRH=Center for Devices and Radiological Health, CFSAN=Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition, CVM=Center for Veterinary Medicine, ORA=Office of Regulatory Affairs), violation categories extracted from letter text (e.g., 'CGMP deviations', 'Adulterated product', 'Misbranding', 'Unapproved new drug', '510(k) failure', 'HACCP non-compliance', 'Insanitary conditions', 'Data integrity failures'), subject line/summary, and URL to full warning letter PDF hosted on fda.gov. Scope to warning letters issued between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2025 (approximately 1,200–2,400 letters depending on FDA enforcement activity levels). Target output: 1,200–2,400 rows, one per warning letter, with extracted violation categories and company metadata. Scraping must comply with fda.gov robots.txt and use respectful rate limiting (1 request per 2–5 seconds).

willingness_to_pay.signal: Four distinct buyer segments with independently validated purchasing behavior. (1) Regulatory affairs consultants: solo and boutique RA consulting practices bill $200–$500/hour for FDA compliance advisory work; a $89 CSV of 6 years of warning letters becomes a core reference tool that supports business development (using trend analysis in proposals) and billable client work (benchmarking against industry enforcement patterns). A single new client engagement from trend-analysis thought leadership yields 20×–100× ROI. (2) Pharma/device quality managers: regulatory and quality teams at mid-size and large manufacturers routinely expense $2,000–$10,000/year for RAPS memberships, Regulatory Focus subscriptions, and similar intelligence tools; a $89 one-time CSV covering the same enforcement data is a trivial purchase that bypasses annual subscription lock-in. (3) Food safety consultants: HACCP and FSMA consultants charge $5,000–$50,000 per facility assessment; a $89 warning letter database demonstrating industry-wide sanitation and allergen control failures is a persuasive sales tool that pays for itself in a single proposal meeting. (4) QMS software vendors: MasterControl, Veeva, and ETQ target companies with $50K–$500K software contracts; a $89 prospect list of companies with recent FDA enforcement actions (indicating urgent QMS needs) is negligible against the average contract value. The absence of any flat-file competitor below $500 (all current vendors sell annual subscriptions or bundled consulting packages, not one-time data files) creates an uncontested entry point.
